judgements.identification: WoM ModManagerSetup.exe 2.20.1, 32-bit Windows game-mod installer with embedded Sciter engine
evidence: entry0 at 0x473a0f reaches CRT startup, main at 0x408a00, and application initialization at 0x435430.
The bundled Sciter/TIScript UI implements user-selected mod install paths, validation, confirmation, install/uninstall actions, and user-clicked error reporting to modmanager.info/log.php.
0x46a9e0 builds wscript.exe with a script path and argument, then calls the process API at 0x46ac4c. Nearby VBS and batch templates implement hidden cleanup of installer files.
The embedded sciter32.dll provides the generic HTTP, clipboard, keyboard/window, threading, and process facilities seen in the scan. These capabilities are retained.

The only suspicious match is VMProtectStub on HookManager and IHookManager RTTI. The same application defines lifecycle classes PreInstallHook, PostInstallHook, PostUninstallHook and validation hooks; none of the eight distinctive VMProtect runtime types are present.

The populated UPX-labelled sections, ordinary reachable entry code, resolved IAT addresses and rejected UPX decompression are consistent with a reconstructed process image. UPX references and layout observations remain.
judgements.limits: Original distribution and deployment context are unavailable. The decision rests on coherent installer execution paths, rather than its collector-assigned filename or a clean scan.
